title: Motor Cortex Cranial Windowing
author: Conor Grasso
materials: Considerations: For injections within the cranial window, it is important to take the injection depth into consideration. Avoid targeting subcortical brain structures, as deep insertion of the pipette into the brain tissue can increase risk of edema. Additionally, maintain bregma as the fiducial point. Avoid the use of multiple viruses/pipettes as pipettes are not made identically (variance of up to 0.8mm difference). Any injection that includes depths deeper than 1mm as being normal to the skull, and depths that are exclusively at target depths of 1mm or less are normal to the cranial window. Furthermore, for the purposes of the shallower injections, "level" is approximately a roll of 16 degrees and a pitch of 0 degrees.
Let Kwik-Cast set for about 00:05:00 before proceeding.
Make the initial incision using a durotomy probe.
Use caution around the sagittal and transverse sinuses.
Raise and remove injection device from stereotax arm.
Replace saran wrap over mouse body.
Detach headframe clamp from headframe carefully.

steps.title: Initial Skin Incision and Exposure
steps.instruction: Prepare the mouse head by removing hair and disinfecting. Create a midline incision with a scalpel blade from behind the eyes to the front of the ears while the mouse is fixed to the stereotactic instrument base.

substeps.instruction: Cut a teardrop shape of skin away using Vanna scissors.
On the left side, remove skin to expose 1-2mm of cheek muscle; do not expose cheek muscle on the right side.
Stop the anterior removal 1-2mm anterior of the rostral rhinal vein.

steps.title: Periosteum and Muscle Removal
steps.instruction: Clear the skull surface of periosteum and muscle tissue.

substeps.instruction: Rub exposed periosteum apart with cotton swabs, bunching it near the skin edges, then cut it away with Vanna scissors.
Rehydrate periosteum if necessary using ACSF dispensed from a 10mL or 20mL syringe with a 25G 5/8-inch needle and a 0.2um filter.
Detach 3mm of cheek muscle just posterior of the left eye using Dumont forceps, ensuring removal is no more than 1mm deep to avoid damaging eye muscle structure.

steps.title: Seal Incision Site
steps.instruction: Seal the incision site with Vetbond to prevent exudate and ensure headframe attachment.

substeps.instruction: Use a Sugi Absorption Spear to absorb excess fluid.
Extend the Vetbond seal 1-2mm past the incision site onto healthy skin.

steps.title: Skull Leveling and Coordinate Mapping
steps.instruction: Level the skull and identify the craniotomy center.

substeps.instruction: Locate Bregma and Lambda landmarks with a Dovetail Clamp and Bregma Stylus; level the skull in the anterior-posterior axis within 0.1mm.
If Lambda-Bregma offset in X is > 0.1mm, adjust the yaw to within 0.1mm.
Measure 2mm laterally from the midline (midway between Bregma and Lambda) on both hemispheres, ensuring medial-lateral axis is level within 0.15mm.
Zero a pipette/stylus over Bregma, then move 1mm anterior and 2mm lateral (left) of Bregma to mark the window center with a sharpie or Dumont forceps.
Mark the craniotomy boundaries 1.5mm anterior, posterior, left, and right of the center.

steps.title: Pre-Craniotomy Injections (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform injections prior to craniotomy if required, following the Nanoject or Iontophoresis reference protocols (steps 8.2.6 to 8.5).

substeps.instruction: Fill any resulting burr holes with bone wax using the broken end of a cotton swab, ensuring no excess residue remains on the skull.

steps.title: Post-Craniotomy Injection Marking (Optional)
steps.instruction: Mark coordinates for injections to be performed after the craniotomy.

substeps.instruction: Follow Nanoject or Iontophoresis reference protocols (step 8.2.6) to mark the site precisely using a fine point sharpie.
Attach the injection device to the stereotactic arm, center over the marked location, and zero the X and Y coordinates.
Remove the device but do not move the stereotactic arm from this position.

steps.title: Create Temporary Kwik-Cast Well
steps.instruction: Build a temporary well to isolate the craniotomy area.

substeps.instruction: Mix Kwik-Cast and let sit for 1 minute to slightly stiffen.
Use the broken end of a swab to create a well around the craniotomy area, allowing at least 1.5mm of space from coordinates and fur.

steps.title: Perform Craniotomy
steps.instruction: Remove the skull island to expose the brain.

substeps.instruction: Remove a 3mm coverslip from 70% Ethanol, rinse in two wells of ACSF, and place it over the window center to align with the 1.5mm boundary marks.
Secure the coverslip temporarily with a broken sterile swab and etch around it using Dumont forceps or a #11 Scalpel blade.
Create a shallow trench over the etch using a drill with FG1/4 or EF4 bits; verify diameter with the 3mm coverslip.
Buff 0.5mm around the outside of the trench using an FG4 drill bit.
Remove any high points of Metabond with the drill to ensure the window sits level.
Drill through the skull all the way around the trench (approx. 20-40 minutes), rinsing with ACSF to remove debris.
Rinse the well with copious ACSF and sterile gauze/Kimwipes.
Place Surgifoam in the well if bleeds are anticipated (especially near the transverse sinus in visual cortex).
Add ACSF and gently pry up the skull island with Dumont forceps; if bone bridges remain, remove ACSF and continue drilling.
Carefully remove the skull island, minimizing pressure on the brain.

steps.title: Durotomy and Hemostasis
steps.instruction: Stop bleeding and remove the dura mater.

substeps.instruction: Stop all bleeds using Surgifoam, ACSF rinses, or Sugi Absorbent Spears; keep the brain surface covered with ACSF at all times.
Remove the dura by cutting along the bone line or pulling flaps with Dumont forceps, avoiding tugging to prevent vessel or sinus lacerations.

steps.title: Post-Craniotomy Injections (Optional)
steps.instruction: Perform injections at the pre-marked coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the skull is level and return the mouse to the angles used during initial leveling.
Follow Nanoject (steps 8.3 or 8.4) or Iontophoresis (step 8.4) reference protocols, stopping at step 8.5.

steps.title: Install Cranial Window
steps.instruction: Seal the craniotomy with a coverslip.

substeps.instruction: Rinse the desired coverslip in two ACSF wells; remove air bubbles using an ACSF syringe or soaked swab.
Place the coverslip into the craniotomy with Dumont forceps onto a cushion of ACSF.
Secure the coverslip by gently lowering the flat, broken end of a sterile cotton swab (or silicone-tipped metal probe) onto the center.
Remove ACSF with Kimwipes or Sugi spears until surface tension is held between the 3mm and 4mm edge of the coverslip.
Apply small drops of Vetbond around the coverslip via an insulin syringe to create a seal; let dry completely.
Detach the probe holder and verify the seal is leak-free.

steps.title: Align and Attach Headframe
steps.instruction: Position the mouse and secure the headframe.

substeps.instruction: Use the laser leveling tool to adjust pitch and roll until the laser reflects back to the center of the tool.
Zero a digital angle finder on the roll arm, roll the mouse to -16°, and pitch down 3°.
Attach the motor cortex headframe via a dovetail clamp; lower it until it contacts the skull without pushing down or cracking sutures.
Re-apply Vetbond to any seals broken during headframe placement.

steps.title: Secure Headframe with Metabond
steps.instruction: Permanently bond the headframe to the skull and tissue.

substeps.instruction: Apply the first round of Metabond inside the headframe and on accessible skull areas, leaving most of the skull within the well exposed; dry for ~5 minutes.
Turn off isoflurane, remove earbars, loosen the nose cone, and detach the headframe from the earbar clamp.
Remove the mouse from the bite bar and place on a heating pad or hold in hand.
Apply Metabond to the outside of the headframe to cover all exposed muscle, extending 1-2mm past the tissue; ensure no Metabond is near the eye.
Secure the mouse back onto the stereotax using the 0° earbar headframe clamp and headframe plate; turn isoflurane back on.

steps.title: Recovery
steps.instruction: Remove the mouse from the apparatus and place in recovery.

substeps.instruction: Once Metabond is fully dry, remove the mouse from the instrument base, turn off isoflurane, and remove earbars.
Lightly scruff the mouse to raise teeth out of the bite bar.
Place the mouse in a recovery cage on a 37°C heat plate.
